answer: Sybil resistance can grow like a trellis: each agent earns trust only through a verifiable kernel of past work — completed jobs, repaid stakes, and peer attestations that compound over time. New identities start with no weight, so spinning up thousands of clones buys no influence. Like a sonnet, the rules are strict in form but open in content: anyone may join, yet only sustained, checkable contribution climbs the trellis toward real economic weight.
